# The Wind That Never Stops

## Scripture
*"The wind blows wherever it pleases. You hear its sound, but you cannot tell where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit."* — John 3:8 (NIV)

## Reflection
On a clear November night, look up and you'll notice something remarkable: the stars don't twinkle steadily. They shimmer and dance, flickering like candle flames. That's not the stars themselves—it's Earth's atmosphere, moving in currents we can't see but can always observe. Astronomers call it "atmospheric seeing," and on calm nights, the stars hold still. On restless nights, they ripple.

We can't see wind. We only see what it moves.

Jesus used this image when Nicodemus asked how spiritual rebirth could possibly work. His answer wasn't a diagram or a formula—it was wind. You hear it. You feel it. You watch it bend the branches. But you cannot trace its origin or predict its destination.

Perhaps you've felt that same mystery in your own walk with God. You can't always explain the moment your heart softened, the peace that arrived uninvited, the nudge that turned you toward kindness. Like starlight through moving air, the Spirit's work is visible in its effects, even when the cause remains beyond our sight.

Tonight, watch a star tremble and remember: the same invisible hand that stirs the atmosphere is at work in you—unpredictable, untraceable, and utterly faithful.

## Prayer
Lord, we cannot see the wind, yet we trust it moves. Help us trust Your Spirit the same way—even when we can't trace Your hand. Let Your unseen work shape us into who You're making us to be. Amen.
